source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 3: Show that: ten determinant identities, parts (i)-(x) (book pages 59-60).

blocks.explanation:
We must show two number determinants are related by the factor 25.
Column 2 (\(5, 25, 25\)) has the factor 5 and row 2 (\(5, 5, 10\) after that) has the factor 5.
Plan: take 5 out of \(C_2\), then 5 out of \(R_2\).
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 5 & 0 \\ 5 & 25 & 10 \\ 7 & 25 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = 25\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 7 & 5 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\)
Method: Property v (a common factor of a row or column comes outside), used twice.

Take 5 out of column 2
\[\Delta = 5\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 5 & 10 \\ 7 & 5 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \(5 = 5 \cdot 1,\ 25 = 5 \cdot 5,\ 25 = 5 \cdot 5\).

Take 5 out of row 2
\[\Delta = 5 \cdot 5\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 7 & 5 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 25\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 7 & 5 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 2 is now \(5, 5, 10 = 5(1, 1, 2)\). This is the right side.

Check (both values)
\[\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 7 & 5 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 3(1 - 10) - 1(1 - 14) + 0\]
\[= -27 + 13 = -14\]
\[\Delta = 3(25 - 250) - 5(5 - 70) + 0 = -675 + 325 = -350\]
\[25 \times (-14) = -350 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Expanding both sides along row 1 confirms the result.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) Show that: \(\begin{vmatrix} a+b & a & a \\ a & a+b & a \\ a & a & a+b \end{vmatrix} = b^2(3a+b)\)
blocks.explanation:
We must show the letter determinant equals \(b^2(3a+b)\).
Every row adds up to \(3a + b\), so adding the columns gives a common factor.
Plan: \(C_1 + C_2 + C_3 \to C_1\), take \(3a+b\) out, make zeros, read off the triangular determinant.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a+b & a & a \\ a & a+b & a \\ a & a & a+b \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = b^2(3a+b)\)
Method: Property vii (add columns), Property v (factor out), Property viii (a triangular determinant equals the product of its diagonal).

Add all columns into column 1
\[C_1 + C_2 + C_3 \to C_1\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 3a+b & a & a \\ 3a+b & a+b & a \\ 3a+b & a & a+b \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Each row: \((a+b) + a + a = 3a + b\). The value does not change.

Take \(3a+b\) out of column 1
\[\Delta = (3a+b)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & a & a \\ 1 & a+b & a \\ 1 & a & a+b \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Property v.

Subtract row 1 from rows 2 and 3
\[R_2 - R_1 \to R_2,\quad R_3 - R_1 \to R_3\]
\[\Delta = (3a+b)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & a & a \\ 0 & b & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & b \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \((a+b) - a = b\), \(a - a = 0\). Now all entries below the diagonal are zero (upper triangular).

Multiply the diagonal
\[\Delta = (3a+b)(1 \cdot b \cdot b)\]
\[= b^2(3a+b)\]
Why: Property viii (or expand along column 1: \(1 \cdot (b \cdot b - 0)\)).

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) Show that: \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & yz \\ 1 & y & zx \\ 1 & z & xy \end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x^2 \\ 1 & y & y^2 \\ 1 & z & z^2 \end{vmatrix}\)
blocks.explanation:
We must show two letter determinants are equal.
Multiplying row 1 by \(x\) turns \(yz\) into \(xyz\) and \(x\) into \(x^2\); rows 2 and 3 work the same way with \(y\) and \(z\).
Plan: multiply rows by \(x, y, z\), take \(xyz\) out of \(C_3\), then move \(C_3\) to the front.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & yz \\ 1 & y & zx \\ 1 & z & xy \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x^2 \\ 1 & y & y^2 \\ 1 & z & z^2 \end{vmatrix}\)
Method: Property v (multiply rows; common factor out) and Property ii (each interchange of two columns changes the sign). We take \(x, y, z \neq 0\).

Multiply \(R_1\) by \(x\), \(R_2\) by \(y\), \(R_3\) by \(z\)
\[\Delta = \dfrac{1}{xyz}\begin{vmatrix} x & x^2 & xyz \\ y & y^2 & xyz \\ z & z^2 & xyz \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \(yz \cdot x = xyz\), \(zx \cdot y = xyz\), \(xy \cdot z = xyz\). The value was multiplied by \(xyz\), so we divide by \(xyz\) outside.

Take \(xyz\) out of column 3
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} x & x^2 & 1 \\ y & y^2 & 1 \\ z & z^2 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Property v; \(\frac{xyz}{xyz} = 1\).

Move column 3 to the front
\[C_3 \leftrightarrow C_2:\ \ -\begin{vmatrix} x & 1 & x^2 \\ y & 1 & y^2 \\ z & 1 & z^2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[C_2 \leftrightarrow C_1:\ \ +\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x^2 \\ 1 & y & y^2 \\ 1 & z & z^2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Each interchange changes the sign (Property ii); two interchanges give back \(+\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x^2 \\ 1 & y & y^2 \\ 1 & z & z^2 \end{vmatrix}\)

blocks.prompt: 3 (iv) Show that: \(\begin{vmatrix} m+n & l & l \\ m & n+l & m \\ n & n & l+m \end{vmatrix} = 4lmn\)
blocks.explanation:
We must show the determinant equals \(4lmn\).
Row 1 minus rows 2 and 3 cancels the letters in column 1 and leaves simple entries.
Plan: \(R_1 - R_2 - R_3 \to R_1\), then expand along row 1.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} m+n & l & l \\ m & n+l & m \\ n & n & l+m \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = 4lmn\)
Method: Property vii, then expansion along the new row 1, which has a zero.

Subtract rows 2 and 3 from row 1
\[R_1 - R_2 - R_3 \to R_1\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 0 & -2n & -2m \\ m & n+l & m \\ n & n & l+m \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Column 1: \((m+n) - m - n = 0\); column 2: \(l - (n+l) - n = -2n\); column 3: \(l - m - (l+m) = -2m\).

Expand along row 1
\[\Delta = 0 - (-2n)\begin{vmatrix} m & m \\ n & l+m \end{vmatrix} + (-2m)\begin{vmatrix} m & n+l \\ n & n \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Signs \(+,\,-,\,+\); the first entry is 0.

Work out the two minors
\[\begin{vmatrix} m & m \\ n & l+m \end{vmatrix} = ml + m^2 - mn\]
\[\begin{vmatrix} m & n+l \\ n & n \end{vmatrix} = mn - n^2 - nl\]
Why: \(2 \times 2\) rule: \(m(l+m) - mn\) and \(mn - n(n+l)\).

Multiply and simplify
\[\Delta = 2n(ml + m^2 - mn) - 2m(mn - n^2 - nl)\]
\[= 2lmn + 2m^2n - 2mn^2 - 2m^2n + 2mn^2 + 2lmn\]
\[= 4lmn\]
Why: The terms \(2m^2n\) and \(2mn^2\) cancel in pairs.

Check with numbers
\[l = m = n = 1:\ \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 4\]
\[4lmn = 4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The same number determinant appeared in Question 1(vi).

blocks.prompt: 3 (v) Show that: \(\begin{vmatrix} y & -1 & x \\ x & y & 0 \\ 1 & x & y \end{vmatrix} = x^3 + y^3\)
blocks.explanation:
We must show the determinant equals \(x^3 + y^3\).
Row 2 has a zero, but row 1 expansion is also short; we use row 1.
Plan: expand along row 1 and simplify.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} y & -1 & x \\ x & y & 0 \\ 1 & x & y \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = x^3 + y^3\)
Method: Expansion along row 1 with signs \(+,\,-,\,+\).

Expand along row 1
\[\Delta = y\begin{vmatrix} y & 0 \\ x & y \end{vmatrix} - (-1)\begin{vmatrix} x & 0 \\ 1 & y \end{vmatrix} + x\begin{vmatrix} x & y \\ 1 & x \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Each entry of row 1 times its signed minor.

Work out the minors
\[= y(y^2 - 0) + 1(xy - 0) + x(x^2 - y)\]
\[= y^3 + xy + x^3 - xy\]
\[= x^3 + y^3\]
Why: \(2 \times 2\) rule in each minor; \(+xy\) and \(-xy\) cancel.

Check with numbers
\[x = 1,\ y = 2:\ \begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 8 + 2 - 1 = 9\]
\[x^3 + y^3 = 1 + 8 = 9 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Row 1 expansion: \(2(4) + 1(2) + 1(1 - 2) = 9\).

blocks.explanation:
We must show the determinant equals \(r\).
Row 2 is \(0, 1, 0\): only one non-zero entry.
Plan: expand along row 2, then use \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\).
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} r\cos\theta & 1 & -\sin\theta \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ r\sin\theta & 0 & \cos\theta \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = r\)
Method: Expand along the row with most zeros (row 2); its signs are \(-,\,+,\,-\).

Expand along row 2
\[\Delta = (+1)\begin{vmatrix} r\cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ r\sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: The entries 0 contribute nothing; the 1 is at position \((2,2)\), sign \((-1)^{4} = +\). Its minor comes from covering row 2 and column 2.

Work out the minor
\[= r\cos^2\theta - (-\sin\theta)(r\sin\theta)\]
\[= r\cos^2\theta + r\sin^2\theta\]
\[= r(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta) = r\]
Why: \(2 \times 2\) rule, then the identity \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\).

blocks.prompt: 3 (vii) Show that: \(\begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ b+c & c+a & a+b \\ a+b & b+c & c+a \end{vmatrix} = a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc\)
blocks.explanation:
We must show the determinant equals \(a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc\).
Adding row 1 to row 2 makes every entry of row 2 equal to \(a + b + c\).
Plan: \(R_2 + R_1 \to R_2\), take \(a+b+c\) out, make zeros in row 2, expand.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ b+c & c+a & a+b \\ a+b & b+c & c+a \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc\)
Method: Property vii and v, then expansion; at the end the identity \(a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc = (a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca)\).

Add row 1 to row 2
\[R_2 + R_1 \to R_2\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ a+b+c & a+b+c & a+b+c \\ a+b & b+c & c+a \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \((b+c) + a\), \((c+a) + b\), \((a+b) + c\) are all \(a + b + c\).

Take \(a+b+c\) out of row 2
\[\Delta = (a+b+c)\begin{vmatrix} a & b & c \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ a+b & b+c & c+a \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Property v.

Make zeros in row 2
\[C_2 - C_1 \to C_2,\quad C_3 - C_1 \to C_3\]
\[\Delta = (a+b+c)\begin{vmatrix} a & b-a & c-a \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ a+b & c-a & c-b \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 3: \((b+c) - (a+b) = c - a\) and \((c+a) - (a+b) = c - b\).

Expand along row 2
\[\Delta = (a+b+c)(-1)\begin{vmatrix} b-a & c-a \\ c-a & c-b \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (a+b+c)\,[(c-a)^2 - (b-a)(c-b)]\]
Why: The 1 is at position \((2,1)\), sign \(-\). The minus sign reverses the \(2 \times 2\) difference.

Simplify the bracket
\[(c-a)^2 = c^2 - 2ca + a^2\]
\[(b-a)(c-b) = bc - b^2 - ac + ab\]
\[\text{bracket} = a^2 + b^2 + c^2 - ab - bc - ca\]
Why: Subtracting changes every sign of the second product; \(-2ca + ac = -ca\).

Use the identity
\[\Delta = (a+b+c)(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 - ab - bc - ca)\]
\[= a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc\]
Why: Multiplying out, all mixed terms like \(a^2b\) cancel and \(-abc\) appears three times.

Check with numbers
\[a = 1,\ b = 2,\ c = 0:\ \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -5 + 14 = 9\]
\[1 + 8 + 0 - 0 = 9 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Row 1 expansion: \(1(1 - 6) - 2(2 - 9) + 0 = 9\).

blocks.prompt: 3 (viii) Show that: \(\begin{vmatrix} a+\lambda & a & a \\ b & b+\lambda & b \\ c & c & c+\lambda \end{vmatrix} = \lambda^2(a+b+c+\lambda)\)
blocks.explanation:
We must show the determinant equals \(\lambda^2(a+b+c+\lambda)\).
Each column adds up to \(a + b + c + \lambda\).
Plan: \(R_1 + R_2 + R_3 \to R_1\), take the factor out, make zeros in row 1, read the triangular form.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a+\lambda & a & a \\ b & b+\lambda & b \\ c & c & c+\lambda \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = \lambda^2(a+b+c+\lambda)\)
Method: Property vii (add rows), Property v (factor out), Property viii (triangular determinant).

Add all rows into row 1
\[R_1 + R_2 + R_3 \to R_1\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} s & s & s \\ b & b+\lambda & b \\ c & c & c+\lambda \end{vmatrix}\]
\[s = a + b + c + \lambda\]
Why: Column 1: \((a+\lambda) + b + c\); column 2: \(a + (b+\lambda) + c\); column 3: \(a + b + (c+\lambda)\). All are \(s\).

Take \(s\) out of row 1
\[\Delta = s\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ b & b+\lambda & b \\ c & c & c+\lambda \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Property v.

Make zeros in row 1
\[C_2 - C_1 \to C_2,\quad C_3 - C_1 \to C_3\]
\[\Delta = s\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ b & \lambda & 0 \\ c & 0 & \lambda \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \((b+\lambda) - b = \lambda\), \(b - b = 0\), \(c - c = 0\), \((c+\lambda) - c = \lambda\). Now the determinant is lower triangular.

Multiply the diagonal
\[\Delta = s(1 \cdot \lambda \cdot \lambda)\]
\[= \lambda^2(a + b + c + \lambda)\]
Why: Property viii.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ix) Show that: \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x^2 \\ 1 & y & y^2 \\ 1 & z & z^2 \end{vmatrix} = (x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\)
blocks.explanation:
We must show this determinant (the Vandermonde determinant) factorises as \((x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\).
Column 1 is all 1s, so subtracting rows gives zeros at once.
Plan: \(R_2 - R_1\), \(R_3 - R_1\), take out \((y-x)\) and \((z-x)\), expand.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x^2 \\ 1 & y & y^2 \\ 1 & z & z^2 \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = (x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\)
Method: Property vii, the factorisation \(y^2 - x^2 = (y-x)(y+x)\), and Property v.

Subtract row 1 from rows 2 and 3
\[R_2 - R_1 \to R_2,\quad R_3 - R_1 \to R_3\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x^2 \\ 0 & y-x & y^2-x^2 \\ 0 & z-x & z^2-x^2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Property vii keeps the value.

Take \((y-x)\) out of \(R_2\) and \((z-x)\) out of \(R_3\)
\[\Delta = (y-x)(z-x)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & x^2 \\ 0 & 1 & y+x \\ 0 & 1 & z+x \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \(y^2 - x^2 = (y-x)(y+x)\) and \(z^2 - x^2 = (z-x)(z+x)\).

Expand along column 1
\[\Delta = (y-x)(z-x)[(z+x) - (y+x)]\]
\[= (y-x)(z-x)(z-y)\]
Why: Only the 1 at \((1,1)\) counts; its minor is \(1(z+x) - 1(y+x)\).

Arrange the factors
\[(y-x)(z-y) = (x-y)(y-z)\]
\[\Delta = (x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\]
Why: \(y - x = -(x - y)\) and \(z - y = -(y - z)\); two minus signs make plus.

blocks.prompt: 3 (x) Show that: \(\begin{vmatrix} y+z & z+x & x+y \\ x & y & z \\ x^2 & y^2 & z^2 \end{vmatrix} = (x+y+z)(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\)
blocks.explanation:
We must show the determinant equals \((x+y+z)(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\).
Adding row 2 to row 1 gives \(x + y + z\) in every column.
Plan: \(R_1 + R_2 \to R_1\), take \(x+y+z\) out, then work as in part (ix) with columns.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} y+z & z+x & x+y \\ x & y & z \\ x^2 & y^2 & z^2 \end{vmatrix}\)
To prove: \(\Delta = (x+y+z)(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\)
Method: Property vii and v, then the method of part (ix).

Add row 2 to row 1
\[R_1 + R_2 \to R_1\]
\[\Delta = (x+y+z)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ x & y & z \\ x^2 & y^2 & z^2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \((y+z) + x\), \((z+x) + y\), \((x+y) + z\) all equal \(x + y + z\), which then comes out of row 1 (Property v).

Subtract column 1 from columns 2 and 3
\[C_2 - C_1 \to C_2,\quad C_3 - C_1 \to C_3\]
\[\Delta = (x+y+z)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ x & y-x & z-x \\ x^2 & y^2-x^2 & z^2-x^2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Property vii; row 1 now has two zeros.

Take out \((y-x)\) from \(C_2\) and \((z-x)\) from \(C_3\)
\[\Delta = (x+y+z)(y-x)(z-x)\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ x & 1 & 1 \\ x^2 & y+x & z+x \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Difference of squares in row 3, then Property v.

Expand along row 1
\[\Delta = (x+y+z)(y-x)(z-x)[(z+x) - (y+x)]\]
\[= (x+y+z)(y-x)(z-x)(z-y)\]
\[= (x+y+z)(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\]
Why: Only the 1 at \((1,1)\) counts. Then \((y-x)(z-y) = (x-y)(y-z)\), as in part (ix).
